messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testIntersectionParallel` creates two `SubLine` instances representing two parallel vertical lines that do not intersect (one at x=0 and another at x=66). The test expects `null` from the call to `sub1.intersection(sub2, true)`, indicating no intersection.

Within the `SubLine.intersection` method, it retrieves underlying `Line` objects and attempts to compute their intersection. The core intersection call to `Line.intersection(Line)` properly returns `null` when two lines are parallel and non-intersecting, as observed in the code snippet of the Line class.

However, after getting the intersection point (possibly `null`), the method proceeds to call `line1.toSubSpace(v2D)` and `line2.toSubSpace(v2D)`. These calls convert the intersection point to subspace coordinates. The problem arises because when the lines are parallel, the result from `line1.intersection(line2)` is `null`, so `v2D` is `null`. Passing this null into `toSubSpace` then causes a `NullPointerException`.

The cause of the bug is that the code assumes that the intersection point `v2D` is never null before calling `toSubSpace`. It should insert a null check after the intersection call and return early (e.g., return null) if no intersection exists, thus preventing a null pointer dereference. This defect is consistent with the bug report describing an NPE in `Line.toSubSpace` when intersecting non-intersecting lines, and the parallel non-intersecting lines tested reproduce the problem.

Hence the root cause is missing null handling after the infinite line intersection calculation before further processing in `SubLine.intersection`.

The fix involves adding a null check for the intersection result (variable `v2D`) just after the call to `line1.intersection(line2)` in `SubLine.intersection` to prevent dereferencing null for parallel/non-intersecting line pairs. This explains why the bug occurs and how it violates the expectations of returning `null` safely in the test case.

This is the complete diagnosis of the failure based on the given test, the bug report, and the relevant source code snippets.

---

Next step: Suggest the method locations to apply the fix.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
